name: Atlas of Living Australia, vertebrate occurrences (species-level counts by period)
licence: per record: mostly CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC, also CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC-SA, CC BY-NC-ND and unspecified (source scan and review: NC about 27% of all ALA records, 9.6% of mammal, 28.5% of bird and 61% of amphibian records); our snapshots hold aggregate counts only, hence tier open
taxa: six vertebrate classes: birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, ray-finned fishes, sharks and rays
time: historical and modern records; 0.34% of the six classes' records predate 1950
space: Australia (ALA country field), including external territories and marine records; records without a country are excluded

name: Australian Stratigraphic Units Database (ASUD)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (WFS AccessConstraints and the eCat record; copyright Geoscience Australia and the Geological Society of Australia)
taxa: not taxonomic; stratigraphic units
time: Archean to Holocene
space: Australian states and territories, offshore basins (OFF) and the Australian Antarctic Territory (ATA)

name: Deposited datasets for Australia's flagship fossil biotas (Ediacaran to Holocene)
licence: per deposit in snapshots.tsv: CC0 (Dryad deposits and their Zenodo copies); CC BY 4.0 (Figshare deposits, the revised Reichgelt record, Gutarra et al.); CC BY with no version stated (thylacine and devil dates)
taxa: Ediacaran organisms, Ediacaran assemblages worldwide (co-occurrence), Cambrian trilobites, Permian bryozoans, Eocene plants, Quaternary mammals, kangaroo teeth (microwear, enamel), pollen and charcoal
time: Ediacaran to Holocene
space: Australia (Nilpena and the Flinders Ranges, Kangaroo Island, Riversleigh, Naracoorte, Cloggs Cave, Tasmania and others)

name: AustArch, radiocarbon and other ages from Australian archaeological sites
status: frozen (merged file of 28 November 2013; superseded by SahulArch)
licence: ADS Terms of Use and Access (custom): non-commercial research and teaching, acknowledge depositors and ADS; sharing of data or derivatives limited
taxa: not taxonomic; archaeological age determinations
time: radiocarbon to about 55 ka; luminescence and other methods older
space: mainland Australia and Tasmania; 75 of 89 IBRA bioregions

name: AusTraits, a curated plant trait database for the Australian flora, with the AusTraits Plant Dictionary
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo; metadata.yml)
taxa: Australian vascular plants (native and naturalised)
time: modern
space: Australia

name: Beyer, Krapp and Manica (2020) high-resolution terrestrial climate, bioclimate and vegetation for the last 120,000 years
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Figshare)
taxa: not taxonomic: climate, bioclimate and potential vegetation fields
time: 120 ka to present: 2 kyr steps to 22 ka, then 1 kyr steps (72 time slices)
space: global land, 0.5 degrees, 59.75S to 89.75N (no Antarctica); exposed shelves included

name: Classic range compendia — Benton's The Fossil Record 2 (families) and Sepkoski's compendium of fossil marine animal genera
licence: none stated for FR2 (Bristol) or Peters' port (use with citation of Sepkoski 2002); the R package is GPL (>= 3); BHL's scan is in copyright, digitised with the Paleontological Research Institution's permission
taxa: FR2: all life, families and family-surrogates (animals, plants, algae, fungi, bacteria), Sepkoski: marine animal genera (26 phyla)
time: FR2: Hadean to Holocene in 86 divisions (dated from the Vendian, about 610 Ma); Sepkoski: Vendian to Recent
space: global

name: Climate-forcing series and event tables — PhanDA, PhanSST, Scotese 2021, Song 2021, CENOGRID, LR04, Rothman 2017 carbon events, Green 2022 LIPs and impacts
licence: mixed: Scotese 2021, Song 2021, CENOGRID CC BY 4.0; Rothman 2017 CC BY-NC 4.0; Green et al. 2022 article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; LR04 NOAA NCEI (no restriction stated); PhanSST's Zenodo release 'other-open'; the PhanDA, PhanSST and Green et al. GitHub repositories state no licence
taxa: not taxonomic: temperature, CO2, benthic isotopes, carbon-cycle events, volcanic provinces, impacts
time: Phanerozoic (PhanDA 0-486.85 Ma; Scotese 100 intervals; Rothman 0.02-541 Ma); Cenozoic (CENOGRID 0-67.1 Ma); LR04 0-5.32 Ma
space: global

name: FosSahul, quality-rated fossil ages for Sahul's Late Quaternary vertebrates
status: frozen since the March 2021 update (GitHub last commit 2021-11-16)
licence: CC0 (Figshare, byte-identical to the GitHub CSV); CC BY 4.0 (FosSahul 1 on TERN); GitHub has no licence file
taxa: non-human vertebrates (mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians)
time: Late Quaternary, mostly the last 130 kyr (ages to about 900 ka)
space: Sahul: mainland Australia, Tasmania and other islands, New Guinea

name: Australasian fossil species checklists (AAP National Fossil Species Lists; Alcheringa annotated checklists)
licence: mirrored: Poropat et al. 2023, CC BY 4.0. Not mirrored: the AAP lists have no licence stated (unclear; treat as all rights reserved), Worthy and Nguyen 2020 is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, Jackson et al. 2024 and Jell and Cook 2025 are closed access. The tier describes what we hold
taxa: mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians, Mesozoic tetrapods, trilobites, echinoderms, archaeocyaths, microbialites, Triassic dinocysts
time: Cambrian to Holocene, by list
space: Australia (mammal list also New Guinea; Jackson et al. also New Zealand and eastern Indonesia)

name: FRED, the Fossil Record Electronic Database (New Zealand Fossil Record File)
licence: no data licence; research-only conditions of use. Public map service header says CC-BY 3.0 NZ (scope unclear)
taxa: all fossil groups: a controlled list of 51 groups; foraminifera, molluscs, miospores and dinoflagellates dominate
time: Cambrian to Recent, mostly Late Cretaceous–Cenozoic; ages as New Zealand stages (NZGT2015)
space: New Zealand and its EEZ; also the Chathams, subantarctic islands, Ross Sea region of Antarctica, New Caledonia and some Pacific islands

name: Geoscience Australia Basin Biozonation and Stratigraphy charts, and palynology zonations
licence: Conflict across layers: eCat metadata says CC BY 4.0 for every record (source claim); the PDFs print CC BY 4.0 on 4 charts, CC BY 3.0 Australia on 1, an all-rights-reserved notice on chart 9 and on Record 2006/23 with its 4 charts, and only a Commonwealth copyright line or no statement on the rest. Mirrored on the metadata licence; no redistribution right beyond what each file prints (CONTACTS.md).
taxa: biozone schemes: dinocysts, spore-pollen, foraminifera, nannofossils, conodonts and others
time: Proterozoic to Neogene
space: Australian sedimentary basins and margins (34 numbered charts)

name: GBIF and ALA fossil-specimen records for Australia and Papua New Guinea
licence: per record: CC0, CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-NC 4.0 (each dataset's licence in its mirrored dataset__*.json); 5.8% of the Australian harvest and 33 Papua New Guinea records are CC BY-NC
taxa: all fossil taxa recorded as FOSSIL_SPECIMEN: mammals, birds, invertebrates, plants, microfossils
time: Precambrian to Holocene, as recorded by each collection
space: GBIF country AU and PG only; Australian external territories (NF, CX, CC, HM), Indonesia and Timor-Leste carry their own codes and are not included

name: Global Paleofire Database (GPD), formerly the Global Charcoal Database (GCD)
status: active online (paleofire.org); last packaged release 2020-10-26; moving into Neotoma
licence: data: CC BY-NC-ND per the paleofire.org terms of use (site footer: All Rights Reserved); CRAN package code: GPL (>= 2)
taxa: not taxonomic; sedimentary charcoal records
time: Late Quaternary; Sahul sites mostly Holocene (median oldest age 9.2 ka), 37 reach 20 ka
space: global; 184 Sahul sites in the CRAN release (Australia 151, New Guinea 24, Torres Strait 9)

name: Krapp et al. (2021) statistics-based reconstruction of global terrestrial climate for the last 800,000 years
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (OSF project licence)
taxa: not taxonomic: climate, bioclimate, vegetation and land/ice/ocean masks
time: 800 ka to present at 1 kyr steps (800 time slices)
space: global, 0.5 degrees on the CRU TS 4.04 grid, including Antarctica

name: Names, conservation status and species traits for Australian comparisons (APC, EPBC lists, AVONET, COMBINE, PHYLACINE)
licence: APC CC BY 3.0 (every row's licence column); EPBC CC BY 3.0 AU (data.gov.au); AVONET and COMBINE CC BY 4.0 (Figshare); PHYLACINE CC0 (Zenodo), with the authors' statement that its IUCN-derived parts are transformative derivative works
taxa: Australian vascular plants (APC), nationally listed threatened species and communities (EPBC), all birds (AVONET), all mammals that lived since the last interglacial, extinct ones included (PHYLACINE…
time: modern taxonomy and status; PHYLACINE also covers mammals extinct in prehistory
space: Australia (APC, EPBC); global (AVONET, COMBINE, PHYLACINE)

name: Neotoma Paleoecology Database, with the Indo-Pacific Pollen Database (IPPD)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Neotoma data use and embargo policy v.2025); dataset DOIs carry a Local Contexts Open to Collaborate notice
taxa: pollen and spores, charcoal, plant macrofossils, other proxies
time: Quaternary; Sahul pollen records mostly Holocene (median oldest default age 8.9 ka), 28 reach 20 ka
space: global; mirrored here as every IPPD dataset (Indo-Pacific) plus every dataset in Australia, Papua New Guinea and Indonesian New Guinea

name: Neptune Sandbox Berlin (NSB)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo snapshots)
taxa: calcareous nannofossils, planktonic foraminifera, radiolarians, diatoms, dinoflagellate cysts
time: Late Jurassic to Recent; occurrence ages 0-151.08 Ma, mostly Cenozoic
space: global ocean; DSDP, ODP and IODP drill holes only

name: OCTOPUS, an open geochronology and environmental database for Sahul and beyond
licence: CC-BY-4.0 for site content and collections per OCTOPUS documentation (exceptions noted per collection)
taxa: not taxonomic; hosts age and proxy collections
time: Quaternary (cosmogenic nuclides to Pleistocene; luminescence, radiocarbon, charcoal, pollen)
space: Sahul for most collections; global for cosmogenic denudation rates

name: Palaeogeography — 26 plate models (the GPlates Plate Model Manager index), the PALEOMAP PaleoDEMs, and Wright et al. 2013 (PBDB's default model)
licence: CC BY 4.0 for 20 models (their Zenodo records) and the PaleoDEMs; not stated in the index for 6 models (Torsvik and Cocks 2017, Matthews et al. 2016 palaeomagnetic frame, Domeier 2014, Müller 2008, Golonka, Rodinia); Wright et al. 2013 CC BY 3.0 (gplates-models-licences.tsv)
taxa: not taxonomic: plate rotations, plate and coastline polygons, palaeotopography
time: Proterozoic to present (the index gives each model a range of 0-140 to 0-1,800 Ma; rotation files hold poles to 3,000 Ma in five models); PaleoDEMs 0-540 Ma in 109 slices
space: global

name: Paleobiology Database (PBDB)
licence: CC0 per the API datainfo and service configuration, changed from CC BY 4.0 in a commit of 2025-02-20; the Navigator page, GBIF and re3data still state CC BY 4.0. Record the datainfo licence with each snapshot
taxa: all fossil groups: invertebrates, vertebrates, plants, microfossils, trace fossils
time: Archean to Holocene; 99.9% of occurrences Ediacaran or younger
space: global; with an Australia and New Guinea region cut from the global snapshot

name: Deposits named by the EPRP question registers and notes — Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, PANGAEA, Mendeley Data, OSF, Dataverse, GitHub and CRAN (global deep time)

taxa: marine invertebrates (molluscs, brachiopods, bryozoans, ostracods, foraminifera, graptoloids, ammonoids), terrestrial tetrapods and mammals, birds (island extinctions), Ediacaran biota, plants and ve…
time: Proterozoic to Recent
space: global

name: Reading Palaeofire Database (RPD)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (University of Reading Research Data Archive); contains records derived from the Global Charcoal Database, whose terms say CC BY-NC-ND
taxa: not taxonomic; sedimentary charcoal records
time: Late Quaternary; Sahul records mostly Holocene (median oldest age 8.7 ka), 37 reach 20 ka
space: global; 181 Sahul entities at 158 sites (Australia 143, New Guinea 24, Torres Strait 14)

name: Sahul sea-level and palaeogeography pack (Pico et al. 2020; Spratt and Lisiecki 2016; Borreggine et al. 2026)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 (Pico and Borreggine deposits on Zenodo); Spratt and Lisiecki via NOAA WDS-Paleo (paper CC BY 3.0)
taxa: not taxonomic; sea level, shelf exposure and palaeotopography
time: global sea level 0-798 ka; Sahul and Sunda shelf exposure 0.1-122 ka; palaeotopography at 45-65 ka
space: global (stack); Sahul and Sunda shelves (Pico); Sunda and northern Sahul to 18.15S (Borreggine)

name: SahulArch, a geochronological database for the archaeology of Sahul
status: active platform; data cut-off June 2022 (latest first-reference year 2022)
licence: CC-BY-4.0 per OCTOPUS documentation and Figshare records; DataCite alone lists CC-BY-NC-4.0, for the radiocarbon v.2 DOI only (10.25900/gpvr-ay04)

space: Sahul: mainland Australia, Tasmania, Torres Strait, New Guinea, eastern Indonesia; locations blurred to 25 km
